report.summary: Checkout does emit error-status spans: in the otel-demo traces metrics it carries STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in every hour of the authorized window, at roughly 16.7% to 29.2% of its own reported span count per hour (6 of 36 up to 14 of 48). So the error signal on checkout is real as a sustained error-status signal, not a single blip. However, the same hourly series repeats an identical 5-hour cycle across all 24 hourly points with no onset, step or escalation, and no data before 2026-11-16T01:02:41+00:00 is authorized, so whether errors are "elevated" relative to a baseline is not verifiable. payment also emits its own STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in every hour with a numerically larger count (9,12,15,18,21 versus checkout's 6,8,10,12,14) and the same cyclic shape, but payment has no STATUS_CODE_UNSET series so its own error share is unknown. jaeger traces_search returned status error (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) on three attempts, so no span parent references, operation names or error text are available and the checkout-to-payment causal link remains a hypothesis, not a fact. Latency cannot be assessed: the only duration metric returns series with no le label and values identical to the span counts. No Kubernetes object identity is available in this target, so root_cause is null.

claims.text: checkout emits STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in every hour of the authorized window; the hourly increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} repeats the identical cycle 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 across all 24 hourly points.

checkout's companion series traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout",status_code="STATUS_CODE_UNSET"} repeats 30, 31, 32, 33, 34 on the same hourly cadence, so checkout's ERROR spans are about 16.7% (6 of 36) in the lowest hour and about 29.2% (14 of 48) in the highest hour of its own reported span count; this is a share of spans, not of requests.

Over the whole 24h window the summed increase gives checkout STATUS_CODE_UNSET = 30, checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 6 and payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 9; no series exists for any other service/status combination in that window.

payment emits its own STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in every hour of the window, repeating 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, which is numerically larger than checkout's 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 on the same hourly points; payment has no STATUS_CODE_UNSET series in the window, so payment's own total span count and error share are unknown.

The 600s rate view of the same series over the full window shows the same stationary values (checkout UNSET 30-34, checkout ERROR 6-14, payment ERROR 9-21) from the first returned sample at 2026-11-16T01:12:41+00:00 to the last at 2026-11-17T01:02:41+00:00.

Metric discovery with selector {__name__=~".+"} in the window returned only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket; no rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, app_payment_transactions_total or kube_* series were listed for this target.

traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket returns series labeled only with service_name and status_code (no le bucket label) even when queried with sum by (service_name, le), and its values are identical to traces_span_metrics_calls_total over the same window (checkout UNSET 30/31/32/33/34, checkout ERROR 6/8/10/12/14, payment ERROR 9/12/15/18/21), so no latency distribution or latency trend can be derived from it.

Label selectors did not restrict the returned series: traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"} and traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend"} each returned the same three series (checkout/UNSET, checkout/ERROR, payment/ERROR), and traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} also included a checkout/UNSET series, so label-filter selectivity on this metric is not demonstrated.

The service_name label values for traces_span_metrics_calls_total in the window are frontend, checkout and payment, and the status_code values are STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET; frontend appears in the label-value list but carries no series among the three series that return samples in the window, where only checkout and payment appear.

The error signal is not an event inside the window: both checkout and payment error series repeat one identical 5-hour cycle over all 24 hourly points with no step change, spike or ramp, so nothing in the authorized window shows an onset of elevated checkout errors.

Hypothesis that checkout's error rate stepped up or spiked during the authorized window is rejected: the hourly checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR series is exactly periodic (6,8,10,12,14) across the entire window with no deviation from that cycle.

Suggested deeper cause: checkout's error spans may be failing calls to payment, since payment emits more error spans than checkout in every hour with the same cyclic shape. This is unproven: no span parent references, operation names or error text are available from this Run (traces backend unavailable) and metric label filters did not restrict series, so no parent-child call edge can be established.

Alternative candidate: the faults originate inside checkout itself rather than in a dependency, since checkout's error-status spans are its own spans and no evidence links any specific downstream call to them; distinguishing this from the payment hypothesis requires the span-level data that was not retrievable.

Advisory: restore jaeger trace access and re-run traces_search for checkout over the same window so span parent references, operation names and error detail can confirm or reject the checkout-to-payment hypothesis; separately verify whether the identical repeated 5-hour cycles in the checkout and payment series reflect real traffic or a simulated/derived metric before treating these counts as an incident.

gaps: traces_search for service checkout returned status error (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) on three attempts (full 24h window, 2026-11-16T20:00:00-2026-11-17T01:02:41, and 2026-11-17T00:32:41-2026-11-17T01:02:41), so no span list, parent references, operation names, error messages or error-status tag detail are available; no call chain or failing operation can be identified.

The span_name label-value queries against traces_span_metrics_calls_total (both with and without service_name="checkout") returned status no_data with zero values, so the specific failing checkout operation is unknown.
The job label-value query over {__name__=~".+"} returned status no_data with zero values, so no scrape-job or exporter identity is available for these metrics.
No baseline before 2026-11-16T01:02:41+00:00 is authorized, so whether checkout's error share is elevated relative to normal cannot be established; only within-window stationarity is observed.

Latency is unknown: traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket exposes no le label and mirrors span counts, so no duration distribution or latency trend can be computed and no latency comparison is made.
frontend appears in the service_name label-value list but has no series sample in the window; its own error and latency signals were therefore not evaluated (not checked, not cleared).

Label-filter selectivity on traces_span_metrics_calls_total was not honored (service_name and status_code filters returned unfiltered series), so per-service attribution rests on the series label sets returned rather than on filter-restricted queries.

Kubernetes identity is unavailable: no kube_pod_owner, kube_replicaset_owner, kube_deployment_status_* or kube_pod_container_info series exist in this target and the kubernetes_state integration is not integrated, so no Pod, ReplicaSet or Deployment can be named as the origin object.
pod_logs and change_history integrations are not integrated in this Run, so no container logs, error stack traces or deployment/configuration change events could be checked as alternative causes.

rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and app_payment_transactions_total were not listed by metric discovery on this target, so gRPC/HTTP status codes and payment transaction counters are unknown rather than zero.
One metrics_range_query call was refused as DUPLICATE_TOOL_CALL and produced no new data; no additional series or time range was obtained from it.
next_steps: Re-enable or repair the jaeger backend for target m0-otel-20260909, then re-run traces_search for checkout over the same window to obtain span parent references and error detail for the status_code=ERROR spans.
Once span data is available, check whether checkout's ERROR spans are client spans whose server counterpart is a payment ERROR span, which would substantiate or refute the dependency hypothesis.

Check whether the repeated identical 5-hour cycles in the checkout and payment span metrics are produced by a synthetic load or simulation rather than real traffic, before scoring this as an incident.
Extend the authorized window earlier than 2026-11-16T01:02:41+00:00 to obtain a pre-incident baseline and determine whether checkout's roughly 17-29% error span share is actually elevated.
Add kubernetes_state and change_history access to identify any Pod or Deployment object whose change coincides with this signal, and pod_logs to recover error text for checkout and payment.
